questions.title: Choosing an interface
questions.text: State **three** factors that should be considered when choosing a user interface.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any three (1 each): the user's experience / expertise; age; disabilities / accessibility; the task (complexity, repetition, precision); the environment (noise, hygiene, hands-free); device / screen size; resources available
scheme.model_answer: 1 How experienced the user is. 2 The task to be done. 3 The environment, for example whether it is noisy.

questions.title: GUI: advantage and disadvantage
questions.text: State **one** advantage and **one** disadvantage of a graphical user interface.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Advantage (1): intuitive / easy to learn; recognition of icons; fewer errors; WYSIWYG; multitasking; graphics
Disadvantage (1): more memory / processing power; slower for experts; hard to automate; hidden settings
scheme.model_answer: Advantage: users recognise icons instead of remembering commands. Disadvantage: it needs more memory and processing power.

questions.title: CLI for an administrator
questions.text: A system administrator controls a server using a command line interface. State **one** advantage and **one** disadvantage of using a command line interface.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Advantages: the server does not need a complex operating system and so does not use unnecessary computing resources (1); can run complex commands / scripts (1); faster for experts; remote access
Disadvantages: commands must be learnt / remembered (1); typing errors can be serious / no undo (1)
scheme.model_answer: Advantage: the server does not need graphics, so no computing resources are wasted. Disadvantage: the administrator must remember the exact syntax of many commands.

questions.title: GUI or CLI
questions.text: Tick (✓) to show whether each statement applies to a GUI or a CLI.

prefill: Scripts can create 200 user accounts at once
Results are shown as you work (WYSIWYG)
Suitable for remote control over a slow connection

questions.title: Resources
questions.text: Explain why a CLI needs fewer system resources than a GUI.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- A CLI only displays text (1)
- a GUI must draw windows, icons and graphics, which needs memory / processing power / a graphics system (1)
scheme.model_answer: A CLI only shows lines of text, whereas a GUI must constantly draw windows, icons and graphics, which uses much more memory and processing power.

questions.title: One disadvantage of each
questions.text: Write **one** disadvantage of each of the following user interfaces.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Natural language (1): ambiguous, leading to misinterpretation of user input; may struggle with colloquial language, homophones or context-based queries; users may need to learn specific phrases; accents / noise
Gesture recognition (1): gestures misinterpreted / unintended; must be learnt; limited commands; tiring; lighting / sensors
scheme.model_answer: Natural language: the system may misinterpret ambiguous requests. Gesture recognition: accidental movements may be read as commands.

questions.title: Processing speech
questions.text:
Complete the sentences.

Speech [[1]] converts the sound of the voice into text. Natural-language [[2]] finds the meaning (intent) of the words. The answer is spoken using speech [[3]].

scheme.mark_scheme: (1) recognition (2) processing (3) synthesis

questions.title: NLI and accessibility
questions.text: Explain why a natural-language interface is useful for a user with a visual impairment.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- The user can give commands by speaking, without seeing a screen / keyboard (1)
- and hear the results through speech synthesis (1)
scheme.model_answer: The user can speak commands instead of reading menus, and the system reads the answers aloud, so the screen is not needed.

questions.title: Privacy
questions.text: Smart speakers with natural-language interfaces may record and store users' conversations.

scheme.mark_scheme: True.

questions.title: How gestures are recognised
questions.text: Describe how a camera-based gesture-recognition system recognises a hand gesture.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any three (1 each): camera / depth sensor captures images many times per second; software detects the hand and tracks key points; movement compared with stored gesture patterns / machine learning model; recognised gesture triggers a command
scheme.model_answer: A depth camera takes many images per second; software finds the hand and tracks the positions of the fingertips; the movement is compared with stored gesture patterns, and when one matches, the linked command is carried out.

questions.title: Gestures in noise
questions.text: Workers on a noisy factory floor need to control a display without touching it. Which interface is most suitable?

scheme.mark_scheme: B
scheme.explanation: Gestures are touchless and not affected by noise; voice recognition fails in noise.

questions.title: Design principles
questions.text: Match each design principle to an example.

right.text: The Save button is in the same place on every screen
A progress bar shows the file is uploading
An Undo button reverses the last action
All images have text descriptions for screen readers

scheme.mark_scheme: L1–R1, L2–R2, L3–R3, L4–R4. One mark per correct match.

questions.title: Choose the interface
questions.text: Tick (✓) the most suitable interface for each situation.

prefill: A blind student searching the web
A chef in a noisy kitchen scrolling a recipe with floury hands

scheme.mark_scheme: Servers CLI (1); blind student NLI (1); chef gesture (1); photos GUI (1)

questions.title: Interfaces in a car
questions.text: A car manufacturer is choosing how drivers will control navigation and music: a touchscreen GUI, voice control (natural language) or hand gestures in front of the dashboard. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of these interfaces for the driver and recommend one.

scheme.mark_scheme: Up to 4: GUI — familiar, precise, but driver must look away / take hand off wheel (1); voice — hands-free, eyes on road, but noise / accents / misinterpretation (1); gesture — no need to look, but limited commands / accidental gestures (1); justified recommendation linked to safety (1)
scheme.model_answer: A touchscreen is familiar and precise, but the driver must look away from the road to use it. Voice control lets the driver keep both hands on the wheel and eyes on the road, although road noise or accents may cause mistakes. Gestures need no screen, but only a few commands are possible and accidental movements may trigger them. Voice control is best, with a simple touchscreen for when the car is parked, because safety requires eyes on the road.

questions.title: Server administration
questions.text: A system administrator manages a company's servers using a command line interface; the office staff use a graphical user interface.

parts.title: CLI
parts.text: State **one** advantage and **one** disadvantage of using a command line interface to control the server.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Advantages: the server does not need a complex operating system and does not use unnecessary computing resources (1); can run complex commands (1)
Disadvantages: must remember commands (1); errors in typing (1)
scheme.model_answer: Advantage: it can run complex commands and scripts. Disadvantage: the administrator must remember exact command syntax.

parts.title: Resources
parts.text: Explain why using a CLI on the server saves computing resources.

scheme.mark_scheme: CLI displays only text / no graphics needed (1); more memory / CPU left for the server's tasks (1)
scheme.model_answer: The CLI shows only text, so no memory or processing power is spent on drawing graphics and more is available for the server's work.

parts.title: GUI or CLI
parts.text: Tick (✓) to show which interface each statement describes.

prefill: Easy for new office staff to learn
Repetitive tasks can be automated with scripts
A typing mistake may delete important files without warning

questions.title: Voice and gesture
questions.text: A smart-home company sells a speaker with a natural-language interface and a TV that recognises hand gestures.

parts.title: Disadvantages
parts.text: Write **one** disadvantage of each of the following user interfaces.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Natural Language: ambiguous, leading to misinterpretation; struggles with colloquial language, homophones or context-based queries; users may need to learn specific commands / syntax (1)
Gesture: misread / unintended gestures; must be learnt; tiring; limited (1)
scheme.model_answer: Natural language: it may misunderstand homophones. Gesture recognition: waving to someone may change the channel by accident.

parts.title: Processing
parts.text: Describe how the speaker processes the request "Turn off the lights in the kitchen".

scheme.mark_scheme: Any three (1 each): microphone records; speech recognition → text; NLP finds intent (turn off) and entity (kitchen lights); command sent to the lights; confirmation by speech synthesis
scheme.model_answer: Speech recognition turns the voice into text; natural-language processing identifies the intent "turn off" and the device "kitchen lights"; the speaker sends the command to the lights and confirms by speech synthesis.

parts.title: Accessibility
parts.text: Explain **one** advantage of the natural-language interface for an elderly user with poor eyesight.

scheme.mark_scheme: Advantage (1) + explanation (1): no need to read a screen / learn commands — speaks naturally and hears answers
scheme.model_answer: She can simply speak to the device, so she does not need to read small text or find buttons on a screen.

parts.title: Privacy
parts.text: State **one** privacy concern about the speaker.

scheme.mark_scheme: Always listening / recordings stored / shared with company / could be hacked (1)
scheme.model_answer: It is always listening, so private conversations may be recorded.

questions.title: Choosing an interface
questions.text: A hospital is choosing an interface for a screen in its operating theatre that surgeons use to view patients' scans during operations.

parts.title: Discuss
parts.text: Discuss whether a touchscreen GUI, a natural-language interface or a gesture-recognition interface is most suitable.

scheme.mark_scheme: Up to 4: touchscreen — familiar but touching breaks sterility (1); voice — hands-free but masks / machine noise / medical terms misinterpreted (1); gesture — touchless, sterile, not affected by noise, but must be learnt / accidental movements (1); justified recommendation (1)
scheme.model_answer: A touchscreen is familiar, but touching it would contaminate the surgeon's sterile gloves. Voice control is hands-free, but masks and the noise of machines may cause misinterpretation. Gestures are touchless and work in noise, although surgeons must learn them and accidental movements may change the image. Gesture recognition is most suitable because it keeps hands sterile and is not affected by noise.

parts.title: How gestures work
parts.text: Describe how the gesture-recognition system identifies a surgeon's gesture.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): camera / sensor captures movement; hand tracked; compared with stored gesture patterns; matching gesture triggers command
scheme.model_answer: A depth camera tracks the surgeon's hand, and the software compares the movement with stored gesture patterns; a match triggers the linked command, such as next scan.

parts.title: Principles
parts.text: State **two** principles of good interface design that the designers should follow.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any two (1 each): consistency; feedback; error prevention / recovery; recognition rather than recall; efficiency; accessibility
scheme.model_answer: 1 Feedback — show clearly that a gesture was recognised. 2 Error recovery — an easy way to go back to the previous scan.

summary: Evaluating user interfaces — the advantages and disadvantages of graphical, command line, natural-language and gesture-recognition interfaces, how they work, human–computer interaction principles, accessibility, and choosing the best interface for a user, task and environment.

blocks.content: The means by which a **user and a computer system communicate**: how the user **gives commands and data** and how the system **presents information and feedback**.
A good interface depends on **three factors**:

blocks.title: Choosing an interface: user, task, environment
rows: Expert or beginner? Age? Disabilities? Language?
Simple or complex? Repetitive? Precise? Visual?
Noisy or quiet? Hands free? Clean / sterile? Screen size?
A car, an operating theatre, a factory floor

items.title: Principles of good interface design
items.content:
- **Consistency** — same layout, words and actions everywhere.
- **Feedback** — the system shows what is happening (progress bars, confirmations).
- **Error prevention and recovery** — confirmations, undo, clear error messages.
- **Recognition rather than recall** — show options instead of making users remember them.
- **Efficiency for experts** — shortcuts, commands, scripts.
- **Accessibility** — usable by people with visual, hearing or motor impairments.

items.title: Measuring usability
items.content:
- **Learnability** — how quickly a new user learns it.
- **Efficiency** — how fast an experienced user works.
- **Error rate** — how many mistakes users make.
- **Satisfaction** — how pleasant it is to use.

blocks.content: An interface based on **windows, icons, menus and a pointer (WIMP)** — or touch — in which users interact by **pointing, clicking, dragging and tapping** visual objects.

blocks.title: GUI — advantages and disadvantages
rows: **Intuitive / easy to learn** — users recognise icons; no commands to remember
Uses a lot of **memory, processing power and storage** for graphics
**Slower for experts** — many clicks through menus
**WYSIWYG** — the result is visible while working
Needs a good screen and pointing device / touchscreen
Can be cluttered; icons may be unclear without labels

blocks.content: An interface in which the user **types text commands** with exact **syntax** at a **prompt**, and the system replies in **text**.

$ sudo systemctl restart nginx          # restart the web server
$ df -h                                 # show free disk space
$ for u in $(cat users.txt); do sudo useradd -m "$u"; done   # create 200 accounts in one line
blocks.caption: Managing a server with a CLI

blocks.title: CLI — advantages and disadvantages
rows: The server **does not need a complex OS / graphics**, so it does not use unnecessary computing resources
Commands and syntax must be **learnt and remembered**
Can run **complex commands** and **scripts** that automate many tasks at once
**Typing errors** can cause serious damage (deleting files); often no undo
**Not intuitive** for beginners; error messages hard to understand
**Full control** of the system and all settings
Works well for **remote access** over slow connections
Hard to discover what commands exist

blocks.content: An interface that lets users communicate in **ordinary human language — spoken or typed** — instead of commands or menus. Examples: voice assistants, chatbots, voice control in cars and smart homes.

blocks.title: How a spoken request is processed
items: **Speech recognition** turns sound into text (acoustic and language models).
**Natural-language processing (NLP)** analyses the words to find the **intent** ("book a taxi") and the **entities** ("to the airport", "at 7 am").
The system performs the action or searches for the answer.
The reply is generated and spoken with **speech synthesis**.

blocks.title: NLI — advantages and disadvantages
rows: **No need to learn commands** — speak naturally
Language is **ambiguous**, leading to **misinterpretation** of user input
May struggle with **colloquial language, homophones** or **context-based** queries
**Accessible** for blind users, people with motor impairments, young children
Users may need to **learn specific phrases** to be understood reliably
Works on devices with **no screen or keyboard**
Can understand **many ways** of asking the same thing
Limited support for some **languages**; needs processing power / Internet

blocks.content: An interface that **detects movements of the body** — hands, fingers, head, eyes — with **touchscreens, cameras, depth sensors or motion sensors** and interprets them as commands.

blocks.title: How camera-based gesture recognition works
items: A **camera / depth sensor** captures images of the user many times per second.
Software detects the **hand or body** and tracks key points (fingertips, joints).
The movement is **compared with known gesture patterns** (often using machine learning).
A recognised gesture triggers a **command** (swipe → next page; open palm → pause).

blocks.title: GRI — advantages and disadvantages
rows: **Natural and intuitive**; no keyboard or mouse
Gestures can be **misinterpreted** or made **accidentally** (unintended commands)
Users must **learn and remember** gestures; they differ between systems and **cultures**
Helps users who cannot use traditional input devices
Works in **noisy** places where voice fails
Needs **cameras / sensors**; affected by **lighting** and space; less **precise**

blocks.title: The four interfaces compared
rows: Good for most; poor for blind users

blocks.title: Scenarios
rows: A system administrator controls a remote server
Low resources, scripts, full control, remote access
Hands on the wheel, eyes on the road
A surgeon views scans during an operation
An elderly person makes video calls
A noisy factory where workers wear gloves
Voice fails in noise; gloves block small touch targets
A blind student searches the web
Does not rely on seeing the screen

blocks.title: Multimodal interfaces
blocks.content: Modern devices **combine** interfaces: a phone has a **touch GUI**, **gestures** (swipe, pinch), **voice** (assistant) and even a **CLI** for developers. Combining them lets each user choose the most suitable way.

blocks.title: Exam-style answers
blocks.content:
**Q: A system administrator controls a server using a command line interface. State one advantage and one disadvantage of using a command line interface. [2]**
Advantage: the server **does not need a complex operating system**, so it does not use **unnecessary computing resources** / can run **complex commands and scripts** (1). Disadvantage: the administrator must **remember many commands** / a **typing error** can cause damage (1).

**Q: Write one disadvantage of each of the following user interfaces. [2]**
*Natural language:* **ambiguous**, leading to **misinterpretation** of user input / struggles with colloquial language, homophones or context (1).
*Gesture recognition:* gestures may be **misinterpreted or accidental** / users must **learn** the gestures / **tiring** (1).

**Q: Define one advantage of a GUI for a new employee. [1]**
It is **intuitive** — the employee **recognises icons and menus** instead of remembering commands.

- Writing "easy to use" for every interface — say **why** it is easy and **for whom**.
- Forgetting that the same feature can be an **advantage for experts** and a **disadvantage for beginners** (CLI speed vs learning).
- Saying a GUI uses "less" memory than a CLI — it uses **more**.
- Listing disadvantages of NLI that also apply to all interfaces (e.g. "it can crash").

blocks.title: Check yourself
items: Name three factors that affect the choice of interface.
Give three advantages and three disadvantages of GUI, CLI, NLI and GRI.
Explain how a voice assistant and a gesture system each recognise input.
Which interface would you choose for: a kiosk at an airport, a server room, a smart car, a VR game? Justify each.
